llm.summary: The skill's description promises a local HTTP proxy and source-level behavior (sanitizers, runner, config) but the package contains no code or install steps to provide that runtime — the claims and the delivered artifacts are inconsistent.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md describes a local HTTP proxy/gateway, TypeScript modules (agent/sanitizer.ts, agent/runner.ts, agent/config.ts), and on-disk files that the plugin will create. However, the registry entry is instruction-only with no code files and no install specification. There is no declared binary, build, or install step that would actually provide a local gateway or the referenced modules, so the claimed capability is unfulfilled by the package contents.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions tell users to edit OpenClaw config, point LLM providers to http://127.0.0.1:8900, and rely on plugin commands (/mg_start, /mg_stop). The doc also claims the plugin will sanitize locally and make HTTPS calls to api.moltguard.com with tightly-scoped payloads. Because there is no shipped code, those instructions are effectively directions to configure behavior that the skill does not actually install — the trust/verification step (the actual sanitizer/runner implementation) is missing, which creates a gap an attacker could exploit in a similar-looking skill.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no code files. The SKILL.md promises a new local service (gateway) and persistent files, but provides no way for the agent to install or run that service. That mismatch is a red flag: either the README is documenting an external project (not included) or the skill expects out-of-band installation instructions (not trustworthy without code/packaging).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables or credentials in the registry metadata. The documentation shows example configs that reference provider API keys (e.g., ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}) and states it will create and store a per-install API key under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json. Storing a plugin API key locally is plausible for the described purpose, but because there is no shipped code to inspect, the data-handling and exact fields transmitted to api.moltguard.com cannot be independently verified.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true or other elevated platform privileges. The documentation says it will create local credential and log files under ~/.openclaw/, which is a reasonable level of persistence for this functionality — but again, without code, there's no guarantee what will be written, how keys are protected, or whether other data might be saved or transmitted.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install or enable this skill until you can verify its implementation. The README advertises a local proxy and specific TypeScript modules, but the package contains only documentation and no code or install steps — this mismatch is the primary red flag. Before trusting this with any secrets: 1) Ask the publisher for the source repository or a reproducible install package; audit the actual code that runs the gateway (sanitizer, runner, config) and confirm network calls and stored files. 2) Verify TLS and privacy policy for api.moltguard.com and request a data-processing statement showing exactly which fields are sent. 3) If you must test, do so in an isolated environment (throwaway agent, no production API keys) and monitor outbound connections. 4) Prefer an install that includes a verifiable build or a package from a known release host (GitHub release, signed binary) rather than instruction-only claims. If the publisher provides the project source and you want a re-evaluation, supply that code or a signed release and I will re-check coherence and network/file behaviors.
